app.title: Monadology Explorer
app.summary: A person picks one of several themes, and a network graph opens with a few starting concepts from that theme. They click a concept or paragraph node to read it. A paragraph shows its full text with previous and next buttons, and every node lists its direct relationships, each with a label. They reveal the selected node's neighbours one hop at a time, or search for a concept or paragraph number to jump to it. Nodes already revealed stay visible, and counters show how much of the network has been uncovered. A separate full-graph view shows the whole curated network with its node, relationship and component counts.

task.text: Read a canonical text through a curated network that links its paragraphs to the concepts they discuss, uncovering the network a step at a time.

data.text: A canonical text split into numbered paragraphs, a curated set of concepts, and labelled relationships between paragraphs and concepts and between concepts. Paragraphs are grouped into themes by number range.
data.item: a numbered paragraph of the text, or a concept, as a node with labelled links to its neighbours

stage.text: exploring and reading a text through a concept network that has already been curated

mechanism.text: A force-directed graph with fixed coordinates shows only the nodes discovered so far. Clicking a node opens its text and relationship table in a reading panel beside the graph, and 'Reveal connected nodes' adds its one-hop neighbours to the graph. Sidebar search, a list of discovered nodes and paragraph-to-paragraph buttons all go through the same select-and-reveal step, so the graph and the reader stay in sync.

field.text: concept-network reading of a canonical philosophical text

workflow.name: explore a network outward from starting nodes, one hop at a time

steps.here: Paragraph, concept, relationship and theme files are loaded and checked. The full set of paragraphs, ranges that cover them without overlap, and links that point to known nodes are all required before the graph is built.
A theme selector resets the graph to that theme's curated starting concepts and shows the paragraph range it covers. 'Reset exploration' starts over.

Clicking a node in the graph opens it in the reading panel. A paragraph shows its full text with ← / → buttons for the neighbouring paragraphs. A concept shows its name. Both list each direct neighbour with the relationship label.
'Reveal connected nodes' adds the selected node's one-hop neighbours to the graph. Nodes already discovered are never removed, and the coordinates stay fixed.

steps.step: find a known item and jump to it
steps.here: Sidebar search takes a concept name or a paragraph number ('35' or '§35') and lists the matches. 'Reveal result' selects the chosen match and adds it to the graph. A dropdown of discovered nodes jumps back to any of them.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Discovery counters show the nodes, paragraphs and concepts revealed so far, each against its total.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The 'Full graph' view shows the whole network with counts of paragraphs, concepts, relationships and connected components.

distinctive: Progressive disclosure: the network starts with a few curated concepts and grows only by explicit one-hop reveals, rather than being shown all at once.
The graph mixes two kinds of node: square paragraph nodes, coloured by theme, and round concept nodes. Hovering a paragraph shows its full text inside the graph.
The ForceAtlas2-style layout is computed once for the whole network, so nodes keep their place as more of it is revealed.
The text keeps its linear order alongside the network: previous and next buttons move through the numbered paragraphs, and each step adds the paragraph to the graph.
